object_description: Cloverleaf-shaped single-storey volume around a central circulation space
design_condition: The compact cloverleaf volume aligns its south-east facade with the street, freeing the central south-east zone for shared reception and public access while placing sports and recreation areas at the foot of the hill.

positive.statement: The project cleverly takes possession of the site through its street alignment and compact footprint.
The arrangement reorganizes the exterior spaces and frees the central zone for reception, recreation and public access.
The built volume clearly expresses the functions it houses.
The central space immediately accessible from the entrance organizes the three units.
The green roof is treated as a true fifth facade and is widely readable from the pedestrian link.
The concept clearly defines three major outdoor spaces.
The supporting wooden frame provides appropriate spans for the chosen material.
Wood and single-level construction are relevant for the poor bearing capacity of the soil.
The project meets fire quality assurance requirements on a single level.

negative.statement: The outdoor activity areas must be physically demarcated for rational use, reducing the relevance of the proposed exterior developments.
The structural system is complicated and its changes in portico orientation weaken the central articulation.
Winter operation is problematic because circulation to the three zones is too narrow or constricted.
The central spaces in the three zones are unattractive or undersized.
The seismic safety device is not indicated, and the cloverleaf geometry requires numerous interior walls to control torsional effects.
A complete second-level extension would probably require deep foundations.
The scheme raises problems with escape-route distances if the building is elevated.
